Sawyer Street Resale: Terms for Selling Goods Through the Shop
Good used household items sold on behalf of their owners
Under this arrangement, an item stays the property of the person who brings it in until it sells. Our staff set the price, attach a tag, and put the item out on the sales floor for shoppers. No money changes hands before a sale. Conditions for bringing goods in differ by category.
Clothing and accessories. Garments are taken only in the four weeks before the season in which they are worn, and must be washed and ironed beforehand.
Books and kitchenware. Sets must be complete, and no more than two boxes are accepted per visit. Label each box with its contents.
Small electrical appliances. Each appliance is plugged in and tested at the counter before it is accepted, and only one testing slot is open each hour. Telephone the shop beforehand so that a slot is held.
Furniture and rugs. These are not brought to the counter. Send photographs and measurements by e-mail, and if the piece is suitable, we pick it up from the address given.
Sixty percent of the selling price goes to the owner. Payment is released only after an item sells, by check mailed on the first business day of the following month.
Accepted goods stay on the sales floor for six weeks. Unsold goods may be reclaimed within ten days of the closing date, and a pickup time is arranged by telephone. Anything left after that is passed to a neighborhood charity. Questions: 555-0163.

Reference: Line BG-300, Larchmont 300 bench grinders
Dear Trade Account Holder,
Draycott Trade Supply has carried the Larchmont 300 bench grinder for eighteen years, and it has appeared in every catalog we have issued. We must now inform you that the line will be withdrawn when the current catalog cycle closes in December. No further Larchmont 300 units will be built for us after that point. --[1]--.

Orders for the line have held up well throughout the year, and demand has played no part in the matter. --[3]--. Replacement parts for Larchmont 300 grinders will remain available from us for four years.
Final orders for the Larchmont 300 must reach our Trade Sales Department by November 30. A changeover credit will be applied to your first Pennington 500 order, but only for accounts that return their old grinders to us when the new units are delivered. --[4]--.

Reclaiming Crate Deposits: Information for Account Holders
Account holders who have paid a deposit on our reusable crates can reclaim it by returning the crates to us. Returns are received only at Hetherton Warehouse, and crates are not accepted at our branch sales counters. The deposit refunded for each unit depends on the type of crate, as set out in the table below.
Crate category | Deposit per unit |
Standard stacking crate | $2.00 |
Shallow tray crate | $1.50 |
Insulated crate (a liner code must be entered on the reclaim form for this category) | $4.00 |
To make a claim, complete a reclaim form with one line for each crate category and the total number of units returned, and attach the signed delivery receipt from the shipment on which the crates were issued. Before a crate is handed to the warehouse staff, please clear loose packing material and old labels from it. You may also add a short note listing any crate damaged in transit. Finally, sign the form and hand both copies to the returns desk.
The count recorded by the warehouse is the figure used for credit, and it replaces the number declared on the form when the two differ. Warehouse staff record this count on a warehouse count sheet. A submission is accepted only when the total reaches 25 units, and a smaller return is held at the warehouse until a later return brings the total to that figure. Deposits are returned as credit on the customer's account, and no cash is paid at the desk. Credit is added to the statement issued in the month after the warehouse count has been confirmed. For this purpose, the top copy of the form is forwarded to the head office to have the credit recorded, while the duplicate remains at the warehouse.
